In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the top quark, if heavy, does not affect electroweak radiative corrections in any way that is not already known.
the standard model is in excellent agreement with experiment, with the exception of a possible small discrepancy in the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon.
the radiative correction effects of the top are completely understood, and that the top mass has not yet been determined to any significant extent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ϱ-parameter and the GIM violation are both small and positive, but not negligible.
the ϱ-parameter is not a very good indicator for the presence of a very heavy quark.
the radiative corrections of a heavy top are very small, and that the ϱ-mass parameter can be determined from the standard model lagranian with vanishing couplings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ϱ-matrix is very close to unity in the limit mt → ∞, and thus the top quark is not a significant source of ϱ-violation.
the radiative correction effects of the top are not very sensitive to its mass.
the radiative corrections to the Z → b b vertex are not suppressed by 1/mt, as is often assumed.
